newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Boardroom row overshadows EMAP H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Boardroom row overshadows EMAP H1.

text.p: Media group EMAP Plc is expected to report a rise of more than a third in interim profits on Monday but a bitter boardroom battle is likely to overshadow the numbers.
EMAP has recently refocused its activities, boosting its presence in consumer magazines and commercial radio but withdrawing from its original regional newspaper business.
Analysts say the strategy is reaping rewards, with pre-tax profits for the six months to September 30 forecast to come in at between 45.6 and 49.0 million stg against 33.9 million stg a year ago.
But EMAP shares have fallen to 719p from 784p in the past five weeks as the boardroom battle has thrown up uncertainty about where the management team is heading.

The fate of two rebel non-executive directors will be settled at an extraordinary general meeting on December 2. The EMAP board is recommending that Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke be removed from the board.
Simmonds and Cooke have led the opposition to changes voted through at EMAP's annual general meeting in July which mean that a 75 percent board majority will suffice to remove directors.
The majority of the board has backed chairman Sir John Hoskyns against the rebel duo over the changes, rejecting Simmonds' call for Hoskyns' resignation.
On the trading front, analysts are looking for a strong performance from both consumer magazines and commercial radio in the UK.
"Paper prices are off 15 percent from their peak last February and the benefits of that should come through," said Lorna Tilbian of Panmure Gordon.
Panmure is forecasting pre-tax profit of 45.6 million stg and interim dividend of 4.3p, up from 3.7p.
EMAP will also see a greater contribution from France where it now has 16 percent of the consumer magazine market following its 139 million stg acqusition of Tele Star S.A. in March.
EMAP did not enter the radio market until 1990 but is now one of Britain's largest commercial radio groups after buying the Metro Radio stations in north-east England in 1995.
EMAP's third main division is business communications -- covering trade publications and exhibitions.
Set up in 1947 as a grouping of 12 regional newspapers in eastern England, EMAP sold that side of the business to Johnston Press Plc for 211 million stg in June.
